Overview

Blockchain & Digital Trust for Banking & Financial Services earns its budget only when it changes a number on someone's scorecard. So we invert the usual sequence: lock the metric and its baseline first, then work backwards to the smallest architecture that moves it — usually composed from core banking rails and the tower platform rather than built from scratch. For Banking & Financial Services, the design tension is specific — instant rails on one side, DORA operational resilience on the other, and a control environment that must survive both internal audit and external inspection. We build for that tension explicitly rather than discovering it at gate review.

blocks.x: Engineering standards & stack

items: permissioned DLT
permissioned DLT — Hyperledger-class networks with known validators; swaps are versioned and rehearsed, never improvised
on-chain/off-chain split
on-chain/off-chain split: personal data stays off-ledger by design; the runbook ships with the first working slice
hash-linked anchoring
hash-linked anchoring carries the evidence path — business events anchored without leaking payloads
notarized audit exports
notarized audit exports — regulator-ready evidence with chain-of-custody, owned by a named engineer on both sides of the fence

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship
Known failure modes, engineered out at the architecture level:

items: Key fragility
Key fragility — guarded because root keys live in HSMs under dual control with ceremony logs; rotation is rehearsed, not documented
Ledger worship
Ledger worship — guarded because a chain only helps where counterparties dispute truth; workflows that already trust one database stay on one database
On-chain PII
On-chain PII, the classic killer; here personal data never touches the ledger; only salted hashes and pointers are anchored
